messages:
Ethan Brooks: Quick RFC follow-up — after reading the notes I'm leaning toward combining three ideas: 1) lightweight reserve API (reserve/release, default ephemeral), 2) small async coalesce worker, 3) conservative prefetch/demote heuristics. Want to capture open tradeoffs.

Maya Singh: Agree on smaller surface. Practical concerns: how do we prevent noisy tenants from gaming reserves and increasing fragmentation? Also need clear operator metrics.

Oliver Grant: Prototype notes: replaced LeaseToken with reserve(key, ttl_ms=120000, mode="ephemeral") and added per-tenant reserve_budget (token-bucket). Benchmarks:
```
workload: mixed-chat+embeds rps=1000
baseline: p95=46ms, cost=1.00, frag_idx=0.30
reserve-default: p95=50ms, cost=0.84, frag_idx=0.36
reserve+coalesce: p95=48ms, cost=0.86, frag_idx=0.31
```
So coalesce recovers most frag impact.

Ethan Brooks: Good. A few notes: 1) coalesce must be incremental and rate-limited (no stop-the-world), 2) reserves must emit preempt notifications so SDKs can rewarm, 3) sticky/permanent pins off by default and behind quota+manual opt-in.

Maya Singh: On preempt notifications: propose eviction-notify payload include {key, reason: "preempted_by_pressure"|"evicted", suggested_backoff_ms}. Also add metric `reserve_preemptions/sec` and `tenant_frag_score`. Alert if tenant_frag_score>0.65 && reserve_preemptions>3/s.

Oliver Grant: Implemented incremental coalesce: async worker scans free runs and merges neighbors, rate-limited to <=200ms work/window per host. Measured overhead ~80ms per pass on canary host (A100, 512GB) and it doesn't block inference.

Ethan Brooks: Nice. Now prefetch/demote policy: propose demote_if(age>demote_after_ms && access_rate < rate_threshold) with demote_after_ms default 120000. Prefetch only when access_rate > prefetch_threshold AND pci_bandwidth slack. Cap concurrent prefetches per-host to avoid PCIe storms.

Maya Singh: For access_rate we can maintain an EWMA hits counter per-key. Cheap memory. Also propose per-node frag metrics so we can coalesce on a per-NUMA basis to avoid cross-node compaction.

Oliver Grant: Ran NUMA-aware sim: if many hot keys concentrate on one NUMA node we get node-level frag. Per-node coalesce reduces p95 tails vs global-only. Results:
```
numa-concentrated trace
no-coalesce: p95=72ms, frag_idx(node)=0.48
global-coalesce: p95=68ms, frag_idx(node)=0.42
per-node-coalesce: p95=60ms, frag_idx(node)=0.34
```
Per-node approach looks promising.

Ethan Brooks: Rollout plan idea: land reserve API behind FF memory.reserve.simple=false, enable ephemeral reserves only. Turn on incremental coalesce on canary fleet with per-node scans. Prefetch disabled initially unless we validate caps. Canary gates: p95, frag_idx, reserve_preemptions, pci_bus_util. Owners: Oliver (coalesce + sim), Maya (telemetry + alerts), Ethan (RFC + rollout).

sre-bot: feature-flag memory.reserve.simple created. Canary scheduled: group=canary-small start=Wed 04:00 UTC. Dashboards: /d/memory/reserve-coalesce (owner: @Maya).

Maya Singh: Action items: I'll add tenant-level frag heatmap endpoint and alerts. Also include guidance in SDK docs: prefer ephemeral reserve for cached prefixes, subscribe to eviction webhook, exponential backoff with jitter on rewarm.

Oliver Grant: I'll tune token-bucket defaults (start with 10 reserves/min) and run heavy-tail sims (Q4_replay + tools/tracegen/heavy_tail). Will also add preemption reason + timestamp to eviction-notify.

Ethan Brooks: Decision: keep sticky pins off in initial canary. If sims show safe frag with quotas we can propose a controlled sticky opt-in later. Also agree to add an idle-compaction path that only runs when host GPU utilization < 20% for >5m. That gives us a long-term compaction safety valve.

Maya Singh: Agreed. I'll draft the RFC appendix with metrics, alerts, and SDK snippets this week. Ping this thread when RFC is up.

Oliver Grant: Will post sim links and graphs here once runs finish.

Ethan Brooks: Thanks team — good progress. :+1:

sre-bot: canary created (id: canary-2026-12-08-04).
